parent.evidence: R0 0.2778 is CLAIM, not a receipt

axis_selection: MASS, CONCENTRATION, SNAP, PRUNE, and RELIEF values are already represented in the reconciled ledger. SPACING has no existing value and is explicitly lowest priority in the brief; TRACKB is Phase-2 geologist preparation rather than a weekly candidate.
support: pinned ancestor H19-5 binary ridge support only; no external data or fault-likelihood feature

common_normalization.feasibility_note: A strict 2.8-pixel minimum allows only 36,718 dots on legal H19-5 support, below R0's 37,654; sqrt(5) is pre-registered rather than silently relaxing a failed selector.

variants.strategy: 4-pixel hexagonal lattice residual, pinned to the grid origin
variants.hypothesis: A grid-phase control should lose credit because Nevada fault traces change strike, whereas a global 400 m hex phase preferentially retains raster geometry rather than the local structural fabric.

variants.strategy: seeded Poisson-disk dart throwing on legal un-emitted H19-5 support
variants.hypothesis: Evenly spaced dots can reduce locally redundant kernel overlap, but R0 was already created by 2.8-pixel geodesic thinning, so a new global Poisson realization is more likely to discard useful ridge-phase information than to improve it.

variants.strategy: H19-5-component geodesic gap priority plus the shared separation guard
variants.hypothesis: At a fixed dot budget, prioritising the farthest geodesic gaps on connected ridge support may extend kernel coverage along a physical fault strand better than R0's row-major component BFS phase.

attempt_integrity.caveat: The durable design record is written before this successful run's diagnostics, but a prior local serialization failure exposed preliminary report-only values. No prediction was revised; do not treat the file as a blind proxy preregistration.
